change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name leaks the website that untrusted_attributes hides from anonymous viewers of TL0 users
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. That is the case for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-59). `website_name` is a plain attribute and is not in that list. Its filter method is named `include_website_name` without the `?` (line 153), so the serializer never calls it. When the profile is restricted, `website_name` still computes from `object.user_profile.website` and is serialized. Before this change, the client built `websiteName` from `model.website`, so a hidden website stayed hidden. Now user.hbs:66-71 shows the host, or host+path, of a TL0 (often spam) account to anonymous visitors. That undoes the anti-spam restriction. Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and delete the misnamed `include_website_name` (the untrusted filter already checks `present?`). Also add `website_name` to the list in the TL0 spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11.

findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the `?`, so it is dead code
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer only checks `include_<attr>?` methods (compare the generated `include_#{attr}?` at lines 9, 18 and 27). `include_website_name` without the `?` is never called, so `website_name` is always included, even when the website is blank or hidden. If the attribute moves into `untrusted_attributes` as suggested above, delete this method. Otherwise rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Same-length host comparison treats unrelated hosts under a shared public suffix as the same site
findings.body: The branch at lines 144-146 drops the first label of both hosts and compares the rest. On a forum at `forum.co.uk`, the website `http://evil.co.uk/whatever` matches (`co.uk` == `co.uk`), so its full path is shown as if it were on the same site. It is display-only and the href is unchanged, but the rule doesn't do what its comment says. Comparing registrable domains, or limiting this to an exact parent-domain match like the `ends_with?` branch does, would avoid it.

findings.title: No test for the sibling-subdomain branch, a blank website, or a TL0-anonymous viewer
findings.body: The specs cover the exact-match, unrelated-host and parent-domain branches. They don't cover the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (line 144-146), a website with no host (e.g. `example.com` without a scheme, where `URI(...).host` is nil), or `website_name` being omitted for a TL0 user seen as anonymous. The last case would have caught the leak reported on line 43.

contracts.action: The website label in the user profile header now comes from the server-computed `website_name` instead of the client-side `websiteName`
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed controller property `websiteName` (`model.website.split('/')[2]`), which was derived from `model.website`
contracts.before_after: Before: the label was the host and was shown only when `model.website` was serialized, i.e. not for TL0 users viewed anonymously. After: the label is the host or host+path from `UserSerializer#website_name`. That attribute ignores the untrusted-attribute restriction because it is not in `untrusted_attributes` and its include method lacks `?`.
contracts.visible_effect: Anonymous visitors now see the website host or path of TL0 users, as text with an empty href. Everyone else sees the host+path when the site shares the forum's domain.
contracts.failure_mode: When the URI does not parse or has no host, `website_name` returns nil and the globe or website block is hidden. That matches the old behaviour for a scheme-less URL.

summary: This PR moves the profile header's website label to a new server-side attribute, `website_name`, which shows the full path when the website is on the forum's own domain. It has one blocker: `website_name` is not an untrusted attribute, and its `include_website_name` method lacks the `?`, so it is never called. Anonymous visitors can now see the website of TL0 users, which `website` itself is hidden from. Smaller points: the sibling-subdomain rule treats unrelated hosts under a shared public suffix (e.g. `.co.uk`) as the same site, and the specs miss that branch and the TL0 case.
